title: A Text Editor With a Cursor

concept.title: Two stacks: the text before the cursor and the text after it
body: A text editor keeps a text and a cursor. Operations happen at the cursor: add text, delete to the left, move the cursor to the left or to the right. If the text is one string, inserting or deleting in the middle moves everything after the cursor, which is slow. Split the text at the cursor into **two stacks**: `left` has the characters before the cursor (the top is the character right before the cursor), and `right` has the characters after the cursor, **in reverse order** (the top is the character right after the cursor).

Now every operation touches only the tops: **add** pushes the characters on `left`. **Delete `k`** pops up to `k` characters from `left`. **Move left `k`**: pop up to `k` characters from `left` and push each on `right`. **Move right `k`**: pop up to `k` characters from `right` and push each on `left`. The cursor never goes outside the text, so use `min(k, size)`. The text before the cursor is the content of `left`.

body.code:
left k:   for _ in range(min(k, len(left))):  right.append(left.pop())
right k:  for _ in range(min(k, len(right))): left.append(right.pop())
delete k: k = min(k, len(left)); del left[len(left) - k:]
add text: left.extend(text)

body: The cost of an operation depends on `k` or on the length of the added text, not on the length of the whole text.

statement: Simulate a text editor. The text is empty at first and the cursor is at its start. Each operation is given on one line: `add text` inserts the text (lowercase letters) at the cursor, and the cursor ends right after it; nothing is printed. `delete k` deletes up to `k` characters to the left of the cursor and prints how many characters were really deleted. `left k` moves the cursor up to `k` positions to the left, `right k` moves it up to `k` positions to the right (not beyond the ends of the text); for both, print the last (up to) 10 characters to the left of the cursor, or `-` if there are none.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has an operation and its argument (a text or a number).
outputFormat: One line for every `delete`, `left` and `right` operation.
constraints: The text of an `add` has 1 to 100 lowercase letters.
There is at least one `delete`, `left` or `right` operation.

examples.input:
7
add hello
left 2
add xy
delete 1
right 5
left 100
right 3
examples.note: hello, cursor at 5. left 2: "hel" is before the cursor. add xy gives helxylo. delete 1 removes y: prints 1. right 5 moves to the end (2 steps): prints helxlo. left 100 goes to the start: prints -. right 3 prints hel.

hints: Keep the text before the cursor on one stack and the text after the cursor (reversed) on another.
Moving the cursor moves characters from one stack to the other.
Never move more characters than a stack has.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
ops = [input().split() for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: The characters before the cursor are on one stack and those after it (reversed) on another. Adding and deleting use the first stack; moving the cursor moves characters between the stacks.
solution.complexity: Time O(total of k and of the added text), space O(text length).
